reason: [SONNET-4.6] sq-qk6ac intentionally changes ALWAYS-COMPILED sparq-engine code, so the feature-OFF sparq-wasm bundle bytes are expected to move. Two always-compiled edits in crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs: (1) `budget::Limits::hit` is re-expressed as `self.why(rows).is_some()`, with the new `Limits::why` carrying the decision and returning the reason string the on-thread `budget::check` would raise; both are `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "parallel"), allow(dead_code))]` (lint-suppressed, not cfg-removed), so the budget module's codegen changes even with `parallel` off. (2) `try_theta_antijoin`'s SERIAL probe loop is restructured: the eliminated/not-eliminated verdict for every left row used to be collected up front into a `Vec<bool>` and then consumed by the cooperative build loop; it is now computed INSIDE that build loop, so a budget-exhausted query stops probing at exactly the row at which it stops emitting instead of grinding every remaining row for a build that discards them. The wasm build takes this serial path (the rayon branch is `#[cfg(feature = "parallel")]` and compiles out), so dropping the intermediate `Vec<bool>` allocation and reordering the loop moves bundle bytes and panic-location line numbers. This is NOT a `vectorized` (or any other default-OFF feature) leak: no feature gate is added, removed or widened, no dependency is added, and no `unsafe` is introduced. The surviving-row prefix and its order are unchanged on the feature-OFF path — the change is that work past the budget cut is no longer performed, which is the same early-`break`-on-budget contract the serial probe loop already documented. NO byte delta is claimed here: the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is not installed in the authoring checkout, so the base-vs-head comparison was NOT reproduced locally — CI leg 2 performs the actual byte comparison, and the accepted SIZE remains governed separately by the `metrics.wasm_bundle_bytes` +/-2% floor ratchet in bench/perf-baseline.json / bench.yml.
